column1: # row_id|proposed atoms (; pv_ prefix omitted)|current slot:id references (;)|specific research disposition / operational definition

F01_10|negative_space_arms;side_by_side||Body symmetry compares actor left/right limb angles and heights; asymmetry changes one named pair. Architectural symmetry hits are lexical false positives for this body concept.

F01_11|negative_space_arms;curled_side||Open shape separates specified limbs from the trunk; closed shape folds them toward it. Split opposing values and do not infer temperament. Expression entries matching open are off-scope.

F01_16|seated_legs_extended;curled_side||Elongation increases selected segment spacing or extension; compression folds the selected segments. Material-compression and file-compression meanings cannot establish a body pose.
F02_02||body_orientation:front_facing_orientation|Thorax and pelvis face the declared camera. Keep head/pupil direction independent; square-on does not force symmetry of hands or feet.

F02_03||body_orientation:three_quarter_body_turn|Thorax shows frontal and lateral planes between front and profile. This is body-camera direction, not a three-quarter-length crop or a fixed mandatory numerical angle.
F02_04||body_orientation:clean_side_profile_orientation|Body lateral plane faces the viewer. Face profile and gaze can differ if explicitly requested; do not substitute camera-side position alone.
F02_05||body_orientation:back_view_orientation|Posterior torso faces the camera. Head turn, visible face and garment back details remain independent.
F02_08|single_support||Pelvis translates laterally relative to the foot base. Hip pop does not alone establish single-leg load, pelvis sagittal tilt, or contrapposto shoulder countertilt.
F02_14|kickback_bent_leg||Name the flexed knee, amount and foot contact; a soft knee may keep its foot grounded. Do not reuse airborne kickback without preserving this contact distinction.

F03_08||hand_pose:hand_on_railing|Forearm or upper arm rests over a visible chair back with same-actor shoulder-elbow-wrist continuity. Railing contact supplies a structural analogy only; target must be reauthored as chair back.
F03_11|edge_sit;deep_sit||Pelvis stays on the seat while torso tilts posteriorly; specify whether backrest, arm or feet supplies apparent counterbalance. Do not force a supine torso.

F03_15||body_pose:one_knee_raised_seated_pose|One knee rises above the other while pelvis remains seated; specify whether its foot rests on seat, floor or is lifted. Knee height alone does not prove foot support.

F03_19||body_pose:reclining_lounge_pose|Pelvis and torso are supported in the declared couch/seat variant; head and foot support are separate. Generic reclining needs exact contact completion before hard qualification.
F03_20|edge_sit||Pelvis contacts the identified armrest surface, not the main seat; record armrest width and visible receiving contact. Edge-sit may be reused only with target changed explicitly.
F03_21|seated_upright;feet_supported_above_floor||Pelvis contacts a stair tread and feet another selected tread or ground. Preserve riser/tread depth ordering; no hidden floating foot support.
F04_02|cross_leg_floor;seated_legs_extended||One knee folds while the other leg has its own stated direction. Do not infer which leg, crossed shins or both feet on thighs from this label alone.
F04_07|supine_knees_bent||Pelvis remains floor-seated while one/two knees flex upward; torso is upright or leaning. Supine knee-bend is a knee-shape analogy only and must not replace seated support.

F04_11|half_kneel||Proposal commonly adds a hand-held ring/box and actor-to-actor presentation to half-kneeling. Half-kneeling establishes geometry; relationship status and prop are explicit narrative choices.
F04_13|squat_grounded;toe_squat||Crouch is a broad lowered-body family. Specify hip/knee flexion and actual knee/foot/hand contacts; it is not an exact synonym for any one deep-squat depth.
F04_16|quadruped;held_transition||Crawling needs one chosen hand/knee or hand/foot contact phase and direction. Static quadruped is a support form; one frame cannot prove travel sequence.
F05_04||body_pose:reclining_lounge_pose|Reclining names a broad tilt/rest family; resolve supine, prone, side and propped support before selecting an exact form.
F05_10|supine_knees_bent;side_lying||Select one flexed raised knee and the torso-side support independently; other leg remains extended or in a declared variant. Do not silently choose supine.
F05_12|supine||Choose back/prone support, then spread specified arms and legs in the image or body plane. Starfish does not force maximal joint range or a precise symmetrical angle.
F05_16|supine;prone;side_lying||Diagonal refers to body axis relative to image frame; first choose torso support. It does not rotate joints or imply a camera lens.

F05_17|supine;prone||Name which supported region remains on the edge and which head/torso segment extends beyond it; required contact and neck continuity must be visible. Broad draped-over-edge has no unique safe or stable geometry.
F06_01|| |Flexion must name a joint and actor side; hip, knee, elbow and spine flexion are different properties. Anatomical angle and camera projection require separate records.
F06_02|| |Extension must name a joint and actor side; straightening a knee and extending a torso are different properties. Do not infer hyperextension or a numerical range from an adjective.

F06_15||body_orientation:axial_elongation_relaxed_shoulders|Describe visible head-to-shoulder spacing and lowered shoulders; do not alter bone length or infer actual neck dimensions from foreshortening.
F07_01|| |Arms descend beside torso with relaxed elbow/finger configuration. Left/right chains and contact versus gaps must stay clear; neutral does not force both sides identical.

F07_02||hand_pose:hand_on_hip|Two hands contact their respective hip regions with elbows selected outward or relaxed. Existing one-hand candidate needs a two-hand variant, not duplication of one hand.
F07_03||hand_pose:hand_on_hip|One named hand contacts same-actor hip; other hand keeps a separately declared role. Contact does not imply widened pelvis or clothing change.
F07_04||body_pose:arms_crossed_stance|Two forearms cross in front of torso; wrists/hands remain assigned to opposite arm chains. Do not substitute partner linked arms or folded hands at waist.

F07_11||hand_pose:hands_in_pockets;body_pose:hands_in_pockets_stance|Hands enter actual pocket openings; fingers/knuckles remain visible when requested. Distinguish full hand insertion from thumb-only hook and avoid garment changes.
F07_14|arms_overhead||Arms extend to selected lateral/diagonal directions. Specify shoulder and elbow configuration; overhead is a different endpoint, not the default.

F07_15|flower_chin;wrists_cross_overhead||Choose which arms create a face-surrounding outline and keep face landmarks visible as requested. Flower or overhead examples are optional variants, not exhaustive aliases.
F08_07||hand_pose:tucking_hair_behind_ear|Fingers contact an identified hair strand near ear; hand and hair remain owned by same actor. Preserve hair length/style unless separately authorized.
F08_08||hand_pose:fingers_through_hair|Fingers pass through an explicitly visible hair region; preserve count, wrist connection and strand-hand ordering. Do not infer haircut or hair color.
F08_10|lapel_grip||Separate cuff fabric pinch from watch-case/strap contact; use actor_1 opposite hand and a named wrist target. A collar grip is a grip-role analogy, not the final target.

F08_11|collarbone_touch||Fingers contact actual pendant/chain rather than clavicle skin; jewelry must exist in the core or be explicitly optional. Record hold/touch role and avoid adding jewelry silently.
F09_01|wide_stance;narrow_stance||Compare knee separation in body coordinates independently of foot separation; knees together/apart are opposing values, not aliases of feet together/apart.
F09_04|| |Specify actor-side femur/knee orientation and visible knee direction; inward projection may reflect hip rotation or camera angle and is not a diagnosis.
F09_05|| |Record foot yaw inward/outward relative to actor forward direction; this differs from ankle inversion/eversion and from dorsiflexion/plantarflexion.
F09_11|arabesque||Specify lateral lifted-leg direction and knee extension with the other support role. Arabesque rear direction is a negative control and must not be reused as a side-extension alias.
F09_13|arabesque;attitude||Specify raised leg, direction, knee angle and support base. High extension does not establish a particular ballet pose, split angle or flexibility attribute.

F11_01|| |Neutral expression requires mouth, brows and eyelids to be separately relaxed in the selected depiction; face-contour or camera-gaze entries alone do not establish all expression components.
F11_02||expression:deadpan_kindness|Deadpan is a subdued expressive convention. Reuse visible restrained mouth/brow elements; remove kindness/character inference from exact pose definition.
F11_07||expression:candid_laugh|A visible laughing form combines open mouth and selected cheek/eye changes; capture candidness and genuine emotion are not provable from that geometry alone.
F12_13|parted_lips;cupped_hands||Specify puckered/parted mouth, one palm near lips and selected outgoing hand phase; a still frame cannot prove an actual kiss or motion path.
F12_15|splayed_fingers||Choose raised open palm and wrist/arm orientation; shaking versus held greeting needs temporal evidence. Do not alias religious abhaya to every open palm.
F12_17|self_cover_hands||Change covering target to named face landmarks and specify palm/digit orientation. Verify actual occlusion; retain any requested visible eye or mouth evidence.
F12_18|self_cover_hands||Select face occlusion and a visible gap around an eye/face region. Separate pose geometry from playful intention, and avoid forcing an extra hand.
F12_20|forehead_touch||Palm or fingers cover forehead/upper face with declared pressure/support role; forehead placement alone does not imply frustration or headache.

F13_09|hair_flip||The cited 2015 hair-twirl usage is a head/hair display movement; winding a strand around a finger is a different variant requiring explicit finger-strand contact. Do not silently choose one.

F14_03|wall_forearm_support;wall_shoulder_support||Choose hand/back/shoulder contact with actual door jamb or lintel; record vertical target and reach. Merely standing near a doorway does not establish contact.
F14_11||hand_pose:holding_bag_strap|Choose strap grip, bag support, opening or adjustment as one explicit interaction; strap and bag must remain coherently attached and owned.
F14_12|lapel_grip;fabric_release||Choose gripping lapel, putting on/off sleeve, carrying or tossing as a single phase. Keep garment presence and coverage frozen unless explicitly changed.
F14_14|| |Choose shoe/heel/strap contact or tying action with reachable hand-to-foot ownership; include support of the other limbs and visibility of the target shoe.
F15_08|kickback_bent_leg||Choose kicking leg, direction and support/flight phase; ordinary standing bent-knee kickback is not all kicks. No target contact or violence is implied.
F15_09|foreshortened_reach||Reach names a limb and target; stretch names the selected extended regions. Depth foreshortening and tiptoe are optional variants and must not be added by default.
F15_13|| |Declare apparent falling, recovering or held asymmetry and the visible support phase. Do not infer actual injury, instability or an impossible frozen center of mass from style wording.

F16_08||body_orientation:axial_elongation_relaxed_shoulders|Combine selected segment extension and inter-limb spacing without altering anatomy/body proportions. Framing and focal length remain independent.
F16_09|curled_side;cross_leg_floor||Select which joints fold and which gaps compress; closed compact geometry is not evidence of timidity or actual body size.

F16_11|shoulder_forward;forward_torso_lean||Choose shoulder protraction and torso/seat support; head position is independent. Do not encode character mood, poor health or a universal single spine curve.

F16_13|wide_stance|body_pose:power_stance_feet_apart|Specify visible feet base and selected shoulders/arm position. Existing covered wording is styling, not essential pose anatomy; confidence and dominance are not observable pose facts.
F17_12|| |Bind two actor mouths or another explicitly requested target, distance/contact and head directions. Near faces or closed eyes alone do not establish lip contact or relationship status.
F17_13|| |Actor_1 mouth approaches actor_2 ear with declared gap and head directions; no actual speech or message can be inferred from a still pose.

F17_14|handholding_pair;pivot_grounded||Bind actor_1 raised hand to actor_2 hand and actor_2 selected turn phase; actor_1 and actor_2 supports are independent. Raised joined hands alone do not prove a completed twirl.
F17_16|cradle_carry;piggyback||Lift is underspecified until carried actor support targets, carrier support and vertical/sideways orientation are named; do not choose a bridal carry automatically.
F17_22|| |Specify which actor properties differ, such as arm height or body direction, while keeping actor count and owners stable. Contrasting poses is a comparison instruction, not one pose.
F17_25|side_by_side||Each named actor inclines toward an explicit group center with independent supports; head proximity does not imply bodily support or intimate relationships.

F17_27|walking_stride;running_flight||Bind one phase and direction to every named actor; preserve count, separate feet and independent ground/flight states. A scenic running entry is a lexical hint only.
F20_08|| |Specify the isolated moving segment and held neighboring segments, then select one phase. One static image cannot demonstrate isolation through time.
F20_09|| |Specify sampled head/thorax/pelvis phase and visible segment curvature; a single curved torso cannot prove a travelling body-wave sequence.
F24_06|tall_kneel;heel_sit;head_torso_opposed||Choose kneeling support variant first, then head/thorax turn and eye target. Look-back does not determine pelvis-to-heel height or exposure.
F24_12|seated_legs_extended;arms_overhead||Name the extended limbs, torso orientation and receiving supports. Full-body extension is a geometric descriptor, not mandatory spinal hyperextension.
F24_15|wide_stance;chair_straddle||Choose standing/seated/reclining support and thigh/knee/foot separation independently. Wide feet and separated knees are not interchangeable.
F24_16|one_leg_balance;supine_knees_bent||Name raised leg, knee angle and standing/seated/reclining base. Foot height alone cannot pick a support family.
